title: Coolant Leaks
summary: Concise coolant leak path for pressure testing, hose/radiator/water pump separation, and estimate handoff.
intro: Coolant leaks should be pressure-tested and located before parts are priced, because radiator, hose, pump, cap, and thermostat-housing leaks can look similar from above or below.
common_sounds: Low coolant warning or repeated top-offs
Drips under the front of the vehicle
Steam or residue near hose ends, radiator tanks, or water pump
quick_checks: Pressure test the system cold and inspect with good lighting
Check radiator tanks, hose ends, clamps, cap, and reservoir
Inspect water pump weep hole and pulley area
Look for overheating history before approving a simple leak repair

diagnostic_path_sections.title: External Leak Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Find the first wet point before replacing parts downstream from the leak trail.
checks: Pressure test and trace the highest wet area
Inspect hoses and clamps while the system is pressurized
Check radiator tank seams and cap behavior

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Overheat Risk Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: If coolant loss caused overheating, verify fan, thermostat, and circulation before closing the quote.
checks: Check thermostat behavior and heater output
Bleed air and recheck pressure after repair
